practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient process-wide (singleton) and avoid creating a new client per request; configure pool parameters only after understanding your workload.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single shared MongoClient instance per process (singleton) and reuse it across FastAPI lifetimes instead of creating a new client per request; configure sensible connection pool parameters (maxPoolSize) via the driver.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool settings to your deployment scenario (serverless: maxPoolSize 3–5, minPoolSize 0; long-running OLTP: larger maxPoolSize and nonzero minPoolSize) and set fail-fast timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS) for production servers.
Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI), never hard-code credentials in source or logs, and keep only an example .env in the repo.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code it or write it to logs; keep only a .env.example with a placeholder in repo.

practices.practice: Keep DB credentials in a secret store and prefer Microsoft Entra (managed identity) + RBAC for app authentication instead of long-lived DB passwords; grant least privilege to per-app users if SCRAM must be used.
practices.prior_belief: Store/rotate the connection string and any credentials in a secret store (Azure Key Vault) and grant the app minimal access to retrieve them at runtime rather than embedding credentials in configuration files.

practices.practice: Always require TLS for client connections (tls=true) and never disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Ensure TLS is enforced for all client connections (use tls=true / ssl=true and require TLS 1.2+) to protect credentials and data in transit.

practices.practice: Enable driver retryable reads/writes where supported (retryReads/retryWrites) and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff for transient network or rate-limit (429 / RequestRateTooLarge) errors.
practices.prior_belief: Use retryable writes and implement client-side retry logic with exponential backoff for transient network or throttling (429/RequestRateTooLarge) errors when running aggregations or snapshot writes.

practices.practice: Provision throughput appropriate for heavy aggregation/snapshot workloads: use autoscale or increase dedicated throughput for the affected containers/DBs, and schedule heavy snapshot jobs for low-traffic windows to avoid RU throttling.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput appropriate for heavy aggregations: use autoscale or dedicated throughput for the database/collections used by snapshot generation (or run snapshots during low-traffic windows) to avoid RU throttling.
practices.source_name: Best practices for scaling provisioned throughput / Autoscale docs

practices.practice: Pick a partition/shard key with high cardinality and even distribution for event collections; avoid low-cardinality keys like acquisition month which cause hot/large partitions.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition/shard key with high cardinality and even distribution (e.g., customer_id) for collections containing events; avoid using acquisition month as the primary partition key because it causes hot/large partitions.

practices.practice: Create indexes that support your cohort aggregation and query patterns — at minimum index acquisition timestamp and customer identifier, and add compound indexes following the ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) rule to cover common filters and sorts.
practices.prior_belief: Create appropriate indexes used by the cohort aggregation: at minimum a time-series-friendly index on event timestamp (e.g., {customer_id: 1, event_time: 1}) and index on acquisition_date/acquisition_month to speed $bucket and range filters.

practices.practice: When using vector search, create and tune a cosmosSearch vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with correct dimensionality and similarity metric; normalize embeddings for cosine similarity and tune build/search params (lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree).
practices.prior_belief: When using vector search, create a vector index using the provided index type (HNSW/DiskANN/IVF) with tuned parameters (e.g., HNSW: m and efConstruction, and efSearch at query time) and store vector dimensionality and similarity metric consistently.

practices.practice: Prefer aggregation pipelines (server-side aggregation) over mapReduce or server-side JS for cohort computations and verify pipeline performance with explain().
practices.prior_belief: Use aggregation pipeline stages rather than mapReduce or server-side JavaScript for cohort computations; verify pipeline performance with explain() and ensure index usage for stages that can benefit from them.

practices.practice: Use explain("executionStats") and diagnostic/monitoring tools (slow-query logs, indexStats, RU metrics) to confirm index usage and find high-RU aggregation stages to optimize.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() and the provider's profiling/monitoring (queryStats, indexUsage, RU metrics) to validate that aggregation stages hit indexes and to identify high-RU pipeline stages for optimization.

practices.practice: Materialize heavy cohort snapshots as compact summary documents and refresh them on a schedule (or with change-feed-driven pipelines); perform snapshot writes with batched operations to reduce RU and roundtrips.
practices.prior_belief: Materialize heavy cohort snapshots as compact summary documents (one document per cohort snapshot) and refresh them on a schedule; perform snapshot writes with bulk operations to reduce RU and client-server roundtrips.

practices.practice: There is no authoritative Azure DocumentDB doc that prescribes using a DB-based lease implemented with findOneAndUpdate for scheduled job locking; this pattern remains a prior-knowledge practice without explicit Azure DocumentDB guidance.
practices.prior_belief: Use a lightweight distributed lock or lease based on the DB (findOneAndUpdate with a timestamp and owner id) to ensure only one snapshot job runs at a time and to avoid overlapping scheduled snapshot runs.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure DocumentDB findOneAndUpdate lease", "Azure Cosmos DB distributed lock findOneAndUpdate", "Azure Cosmos DB job lease pattern"

practices.practice: Project only required fields early in aggregation pipelines ($project before expensive stages) to reduce network bandwidth and RU consumption.
practices.prior_belief: Limit fields returned by queries and aggregation ($project early) to only those required by the API to reduce network bandwidth and RU consumption (project before expensive stages when possible).

practices.practice: Embed frequently-read attributes (channel, product) in event documents to avoid expensive $lookup joins; if joins are required, denormalise or precompute the join results.
practices.prior_belief: Design the events schema to embed frequently-accessed attributes (channel, product) inside event documents to avoid $lookup joins; if joins are required, ensure joined fields are indexed and pipeline uses $lookup efficiently or precompute denormalized snapshots.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral data (e.g., raw telemetry) to automatically expire old documents and control storage growth and RU costs.
practices.prior_belief: Add TTL indexes for ephemeral event data that can be expired (e.g., raw telemetry older than X days) to control storage growth and reduce long-term RU costs.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB's MongoDB API feature-support pages indicate $bucket and $bucketAuto are not supported for many API-server versions; instead avoid building pipelines that rely on unsupported stages — compute boundaries client-side or use materialized/streaming approaches to bound group cardinality.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid large in-memory accumulations in the aggregation pipeline (unbounded $group outputs) — use $bucket/$bucketAuto to bound group cardinality and consider incremental snapshotting for extremely large datasets.
practices.source_name: Azure Cosmos DB feature support (MongoDB) / aggregation pipeline pages

practices.practice: When the account capability EnableMongoRetryableWrites is enabled, bulk unordered writes are not supported; perform ordered bulk writes or disable retryable-writes if you need unordered bulk semantics.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulkWrite with ordered=False for inserting/updating many documents (snapshot materialisation) to maximize throughput and reduce RU costs; handle duplicate-key errors or transient failures explicitly.
practices.source_name: Azure Cosmos DB feature support (retryable writes)
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB retryable writes bulk unordered unsupported"

practices.practice: Restrict network access to the cluster using firewall rules, VNet/Private Endpoint and disable public network access for production clusters.
practices.prior_belief: Restrict network access to the DocumentDB cluster using firewall rules, VNet integration or private endpoints; do not expose the cluster to the public internet without access controls.

practices.practice: Instrument the service with application-level metrics (snapshot duration, RU consumed per snapshot, aggregation latencies) and alert on RU throttling, repeated failures, or resource saturation.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument the service to collect application-level metrics (snapshot duration, RU consumed per snapshot, aggregation latencies) and alert on RU throttling, high latency, or repeated failures so snapshots and API reliability can be monitored and tuned.

practices.practice: Do not rely on client-specified MongoDB writeConcern; Azure DocumentDB maps/controls durability via account consistency and handles replication (writes are quorum by default); client writeConcern may be ignored.
practices.prior_belief: Set a safe write concern and reasonable wtimeout for critical writes (snapshot writes) and handle write concern errors; do not assume default fire-and-forget semantics for important materialized snapshot persistence.
practices.source_name: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB feature support — write concern mapping

practices.practice: For aggregation facets (channel/product breakdown), design compound indexes that match equality and group keys following the ESR rule to reduce scanned documents and RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: When designing indexes for aggregation facets (channel/product breakdown), consider compound indexes that support both the match/filter and the group keys to reduce in-pipeline scanning and RU cost.

practices.practice: There is little explicit Azure DocumentDB public guidance about enforcing collection-level JSON schema validators for the MongoDB API; while JSON-schema query/operators exist, explicit collection validator support is not clearly documented for all MongoDB API versions.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce a JSON schema or document validation rules on collections (customers, events, cohort_snapshots) to catch malformed documents early and keep aggregation assumptions stable.
practices.how_found: searches: "Azure Cosmos DB MongoDB collection validator", "$jsonSchema operator Azure Cosmos DB", "Azure DocumentDB collection schema validation"

practices.practice: Prefer incremental or change-feed / event-driven snapshot updates (update only changed cohorts) rather than full recomputes for large datasets; use materialized views / Stream Analytics or change-feed-driven pipelines to keep snapshots fresh with lower RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer incremental or rolling snapshot updates (update only changed cohorts) rather than full recomputes when datasets are large, to reduce RU usage and snapshot run time.
practices.source_name: Improve efficiency of reads by using a cache / materialize via Stream Analytics and change feed
practices.how_found: search: "materialize data Azure Cosmos DB change feed Stream Analytics"

practices.practice: Check the Azure Cosmos DB feature-support pages for the API-for-MongoDB server-version you run; aggregation-stage support and other operators vary by server version and features (e.g., some stages are unsupported on particular versions).
practices.source_name: Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB feature support pages

notes: I inspected the app and loaded multiple installed skills (documentdb-*) plus Microsoft Learn pages. Most prior beliefs from general MongoDB and Cosmos guidance were confirmed by Azure DocumentDB docs or installed skills. Key contradictions: (1) bulk unordered writes can be disallowed when the server-side retryable-writes capability is enabled — Azure docs explicitly warn unordered bulk writes aren't supported in that mode; (2) client writeConcern is ignored / mapped by the service, so don't rely on setting custom client writeConcern for durability; (3) the $bucket/$bucketAuto aggregation stages are not supported in many MongoDB API server versions according to the Azure feature-support pages, so pipelines relying on them may not run on Azure DocumentDB; use alternative bucketing or materialized/stream approaches. Where guidance came from an installed skill I listed the skill name in how_found; where it came from Microsoft Learn I used the search or query that found the page and included the exact URL from the tool result.
